question: Prediction of conversion from MCI to AD within 3 years (36 months), from baseline data, in ADNI MCI participants. Both models are multimodal and share the clinical/cognitive channel. P-81 uses CDR-SB, logical memory delayed recall, MMSE, mPACC digit and mPACC trails B, plus age and FDG-PET. P-8 uses MMSE, CDR-SB and ADAS-cog, plus age, sex, APOE4, FreeSurfer volumes and T1 MRI. The imaging channel differs (PET vs MRI), but both papers also report a model on cognitive scores alone, which gives a same-channel pair.
metric: AUC with AUC (0.785 vs 0.874). Balanced accuracy with balanced accuracy: P-81 reports BA 0.733, and P-8's BA from its sensitivity 0.85 and specificity 0.78 is 0.815 (its plain accuracy is 81.34% on near-balanced classes).

figures.P-81: PET+Age+CS, 5-fold CV over 257 MCI (93 converters/164 stable): AUC 0.7849 +/- 0.0963 and BA 0.7326 +/- 0.0978 (fold SDs; no interval reported). Hanley-McNeil with A=0.785: Q1=A/(2-A)=0.646 and Q2=2A^2/(1+A)=0.690, so SE=sqrt([A(1-A)+92(Q1-A^2)+163(Q2-A^2)]/(93*164))=0.031 and the 95% CI is 0.723-0.846. BA Wilson (p=0.733, n=257): 0.675-0.783. Cognitive scores alone (CS): AUC 0.7496 +/- 0.0683, HM SE 0.033, CI 0.685-0.815; BA 0.7130 +/- 0.0589, Wilson 0.655-0.765.
figures.P-8: DAFN, 5-fold CV over 593 MCI (295 pMCI/298 sMCI): accuracy 81.34%, AUC 0.874 (fold variance 0.001), sensitivity 0.85, specificity 0.78 (BA 0.815). HM SE 0.015 gives an AUC CI of 0.845-0.903. Accuracy Wilson (n=593): 0.780-0.843; BA Wilson: 0.782-0.844. Cognitive-SVM (MMSE, CDR-SB, ADAS-cog): accuracy 77.24%, AUC 0.832, sensitivity 0.75, specificity 0.79 (BA 0.77); HM SE 0.017, CI 0.799-0.865; BA Wilson 0.735-0.802. Meta All-SVM (all metadata, no image): 78.75%, AUC 0.868.

matched_figure_check: Neither paper uses the other's imaging modality. On the shared channel, the matched figure is each paper's cognitive-scores-only model: P-81 has AUC 0.750 and BA 0.713, and P-8 has AUC 0.832 and BA 0.77. These do not agree within uncertainty. P-81's 0.750 lies outside P-8's HM interval (0.799-0.865), and P-8's 0.832 lies outside P-81's (0.685-0.815). The matched figures therefore reproduce the gap on the shared channel rather than dissolving it.
performance_validity: Neither study reaches 0.97 on the conversion task. P-81's 1.000 values are for AD vs CN with cognitive scores, which the authors attribute to scores used to define AD; that is not the compared task. Both use internal 5-fold CV only.

candidate_explanations.difference: Imaging modality: whole-brain FDG-PET (P-81) vs T1 structural MRI (P-8). Both papers show imaging adds little to the non-imaging inputs, so this is not shown to carry the gap.
candidate_explanations.quote: Neurocognitive scores predicted better than FDG-PET per se, but the best model was a combination of FDG-PET, age, and neurocognitive data

candidate_explanations.difference: Different cognitive instruments: P-8 includes ADAS-cog, while P-81 uses logical memory delayed recall and two mPACC variants. The cognitive-only gap (AUC 0.750 vs 0.832) sits in this channel.
candidate_explanations.quote: The baseline cognitive test scores consist of MMSE, CDR-SB, and ADAS-cog.

candidate_explanations.difference: Additional non-imaging predictors in P-8 (APOE4 and seven FreeSurfer volumes); its metadata-only SVM already reaches AUC 0.868.
candidate_explanations.quote: For volumetric data, we retrieved post-processed MRI information from the ADNI dataset which contains measurements of the Ventricles, Hippocampus, Whole brain, Entorhinal cortex, Fusiform gyrus, Middle temporal gyrus (MidTemp), and Intracranial Volume (ICV).

candidate_explanations.difference: Cohort and class balance: 257 MCI with 36% converters (ADNI1/2/GO with FDG-PET within two months of diagnosis) vs 593 MCI with 50% converters (ADNI1/2, Wen et al. splits). Balance affects accuracy more than AUC.
Label definition: P-8 requires the MCI diagnosis to remain stable over 36 months, while P-81 labels non-converters within three years as stable without stating a follow-up requirement.
candidate_explanations.quote: (2) stable MCI (sMCI) if the patient’s diagnosis remains as MCI over the same time period.

candidate_explanations.difference: Model and sample size for the cognitive-only arm: a small dense network fitted on 257 subjects (P-81) vs an SVM on 593 subjects (P-8).
candidate_explanations.quote: The input arrays are sent through a series of four Dense layers of filter size 8, 16, 16, and 32, followed by a sigmoid activation.

reason: Both papers predict 3-year MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI with multimodal models that share the cognitive-score channel, and both report cognitive-only models. The headline AUCs (0.785 vs 0.874) each lie outside the other's Hanley-McNeil interval, and so do the cognitive-only AUCs (0.750 vs 0.832), so the gap is beyond uncertainty on the shared channel as well as on the full models. Imaging modality, cognitive instruments, added predictors, converter proportion, label definition and sample size are candidate explanations; neither paper shows any of them to be sufficient. Sensitivity: with P-81's fold SDs instead of Hanley-McNeil (t, 4 df), P-81's interval widens to 0.665-0.904 and contains 0.874. P-81's 0.785 still lies outside P-8's fold-based interval (0.874 +/- 2.776*0.0316/sqrt(5) = 0.835-0.913), so the one-directional criterion still holds. Both cohorts come from ADNI, so subjects may overlap in part.

quotes.quote: Neurocognitive scores predicted better than FDG-PET per se, but the best model was a combination of FDG-PET, age, and neurocognitive data, yielding an AUC of 0.785 ± 0.096 and a balanced accuracy of 0.733 ± 0.098.
